sections.title: Tamil in the Internet Age
sections.content:
Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and a living language for thousands of years. The development of modern technology does not affect Tamil's growth — it is ready to adopt technological changes.

**Tamil on the Internet:**
- A 2017 study by KPMG (Singapore) with Google found that **Tamil topped the list** of the most widely used regional languages in India, with **42% of Indian internet users** using the internet in Tamil.
- By 2021, **74% of people in India** were predicted to access the internet using Tamil, making it the top internet language in India.
- **Google and Bing** both provide searching facilities in Tamil. Google's search engine includes a built-in Tamil virtual keyboard.

---

**e-Governance in Tamil:**
Getting government services through the internet is known as **e-Governance**. The Government of Tamil Nadu provides all its services through the internet in Tamil. Citizens can communicate with the government from anywhere in the world.

Key Tamil e-Governance websites:
- Official Website of Govt. of Tamil Nadu: http://www.tn.gov.in/ta
- Directorate of Government Examinations: http://www.dge.tn.nic.in/
- Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC): http://www.tnpsc.gov.in/tamilversion/
- Outside India: The **Government of Sri Lanka** also provides all services in Tamil.

---

**e-Library in Tamil:**
Tamil e-Library portals provide thousands of Tamil books as e-books, mostly free of cost — especially useful for Tamil people living far from their homeland.

Key Tamil e-Libraries:
- Tamilnadu School Education Textbooks: http://www.textbooksonline.tn.nic.in/
- Tamil Virtual Academy Library: http://www.tamilvu.org/library/
- Tamil Digital Library: http://tamildigitallibrary.in/
- Project Madurai: http://www.projectmadurai.org/
- Anna Centenary Library: http://www.annacentenarylibrary.org/

sections.title: Tamil Software, Encoding and Organisations
sections.content:
**Tamil Typing Interface Software:**
Tamil can be typed using keyboard interface software that works on Tamil Unicode with phonetics:
- **NHM Writer, E-Kalappai, Lippikar** — familiar Tamil keyboard interface software for computers.
- **Sellinam and Ponmadal** — familiar Tamil keyboard layouts for Android smartphones.

**Tamil Office Automation Applications:**
- Microsoft Office, LibreOffice, and OpenOffice provide complete Tamil interface facilities.
- After installation, menus, icons, dialog boxes, and commands appear in Tamil. Files and folders can be saved with Tamil names.
- Dedicated Tamil applications: Tamil LibreOffice, Tamil OpenOffice, Azhagi Unicode Editor, Ponmozhi, Menthamizh, Kamban, Vani.

**Tamil Translation:**
- **Thamizpori (தமிழ்பொறி)** — a Tamil translation application with over 30,000 Tamil word equivalents for English words. Can translate small English sentences to Tamil.
- **Google Translate** also provides online Tamil translation.

**Tamil Programming Language:**
- Programming languages are traditionally available only in English.
- The first Tamil programming language, **"Ezhil" (எழில்)**, was designed based on the Python programming language.

---

**Tamil Information Interchange Coding Systems:**

**TSCII (Tamil Script Code for Information Interchange):**
The first coding system designed to handle Tamil language. Registered in **IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority)** — a unit of ICANN.

**ISCII (Indian Script Code for Information Interchange):**
An encoding scheme designed for Indian languages including Tamil. Unified with Unicode.

**Unicode:**
An encoding system designed to handle various world languages, including Tamil. Its first version **1.0.0** was introduced in **October 1991**. Unicode is the best suitable system to handle Tamil.

---

**Tamil Operating System:**
All operating systems (Windows, Linux, Android) are available with Tamil environment interfaces. The Windows Tamil Environment interface can be downloaded and installed — it displays taskbar, desktop icons, commands, and menus in Tamil.

---

**Organisations and Projects:**

**Tamil Virtual Academy:**
Established on **17th February 2001** by the Government of Tamil Nadu. Objective: spread Tamil to the entire world through the internet. Offers courses in Tamil language, culture, and heritage from kindergarten to undergraduate level. Website: http://www.tamilvu.org/

**Tamil Language Council, Singapore:**
Formed in **2001** by the Ministry of Information, Communications and Arts, Government of Singapore. Called **"வளர்தமிழ் இயக்கம்"**. Promotes awareness and greater use of Tamil among Singaporeans.

**Project Madurai:**
An open and voluntary initiative to collect and publish free electronic editions of ancient Tamil literary classics (e-texts). Launched in **1998**. e-texts released in TSCII encoding; since 2004 also in Tamil Unicode. Website: http://www.projectmadurai.org/

**Tamil Wikipedia:**
Wikipedia is an open-source encyclopaedia where anyone can write articles. Tamil Wikipedia has more than **one lakh (100,000) articles**. Website: https://ta.wikipedia.org/
